title.narrative: Go-For Expanding space for youth's political participation
Go-For Utöka utrymmet för ungdomars politiska deltagande

description.narrative: The projects goal is to expand the space for political youth participation in decision making processes in Türkiye. The project will be implemented by GoFor in partnership with LSU of Sweden. The project aims to address two problems: the absence of a structured mechanism for youth political participation and non-inclusive practices that prevent young people from participating. Whereby addressing these issues aims to increase the demand of youth participation, transform participation mechanisms, and change decisionmakers' attitudes towards including young people in the long term. The project has identified two main objectives: to strengthen the capacities of youth organizations to increase youth participation in decisionmaking processes to develop relationships with local decisionmakers to mainstream youth rights at the local level

Projektets mål är att utöka utrymmet för politiska ungdomars deltagande i beslutsprocesser i Turkiet. Projektet kommer att genomföras av GoFor i samarbete med LSU of Sweden.
Projektet syftar till att lösa två utvecklingsutmaningar; Avsaknaden av en strukturerad mekanism för politiskt deltagande för ungdomar och icke-inkluderande metoder som hindrar unga människor från att delta.
Att ta itu med dessa frågor syftar till att öka efterfrågan på ungdomars deltagande, förändra deltagandemekanismer och förändra beslutsfattares attityder inkludera ungdomar på lång sikt.

The projects goal is to expand the space for political youth participation in decision­ making processes in Türkiye. The project will be implemented by GoFor in partnership with LSU of Sweden. The project aims to address two problems: the absence of a structured mechanism for youth political participation and non-inclusive practices that prevent young people from participating. Whereby addressing these issues aims to increase the demand of youth participation, transform participation mechanisms, and change decision­makers' attitudes towards including young people in the long term.

Based on progress so far, GoFor's two strategic objectives are assessed to be broadly on track but will depend on effective delivery and follow-up in 2025 and 2026 to fully achieve their goals.
Objective 1 (Strengthening Youth Organizations Capacities) has a moderately high likelihood of success. In 2024, GoFor expanded its adhoc support, meeting diverse member needs and delivering some concrete funding wins. The Youth Expert Pool was well-designed with strong demand confirmed, but actual deployment was postponed, making its impact untested until 2025. Knowledge-sharing activities, including the Members Forum, Needs Assessment, and General Assembly, helped strengthen member voice and leadership diversity. GoFor also significantly increased its national and international recognition, exceeding initial expectations.
However, challenges remain. The effectiveness of the Expert Pool will only be proven through visible capacity gains for member organizations. Additionally, it remains to be seen whether ideas developed in forums will translate into real organizational changes. Achieving objective 1 will depend on continued capacity improvements across the network.
Objective 2 (Fostering Relationships with Local Decision-Makers) is feasible but more uncertain given political risks. In 2024, GoFor signed formal agreements with three municipalities, launched or revitalized youth councils, and began drafting local Youth Strategies with youth input. Municipal buy-in was demonstrated through co-funding for planned 2025 training camps. The election campaign (#KaçGençVar?) raised youth issues in public debate, secured 88 candidate pledges, and fostered new dialogue with duty-bearers, while the Youth Political Preferences Research offered a credible advocacy tool.
Still, these results are mainly outputs or early outcomes. The real test will be in 2025: whether youth councils function effectively, youth strategies are completed and approved, and authorities act on youth input. The broader political environment remains a risk, particularly for opposition-run municipalities that could face central government intervention. Safeguarding challenges and reputational attacks also remain concerns.
Overall, both objectives appear achievable if planned activities for the rest of the project are delivered effectively
